**STEP 1 - Scene:** A breakfast tray with two slices of toast on a white paper plate. The tea, juice, and butter portions sit on the tray, not on the plate, so they are not part of this plated meal.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** White paper plate, about 20 cm diameter. Area = 3.14 × (10)² ≈ 314 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Two stacked slices of toast (wholemeal-style, lightly browned). No visible oil or spread on the plate.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The two stacked slices cover roughly 35% of the plate (about 110 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Two stacked slices, about 2 cm envelope height. 110 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 220 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Toast is airy, so I use a bread-like density of about 0.3 g/ml, which matches a real slice weighing about 30 g. 220 ml × 0.3 ≈ 66 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Toasted bread is about 250 kcal/100 g. 66 g × 2.5 ≈ 165 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two slices of toast weighing about 66 g and about 165 kcal is plausible. The butter packets and drinks are excluded because they are off the plate. Total on-plate estimate: about 66 g, about 165 kcal.
